header: When does an Executive Deep Synthesis answer need a WIDER omnibar box? A comparison table of 4 or more columns (the parameter and three entities or periods) is cramped in the normal width, so I widen the box while such a table is on the screen and return it to its normal width the moment the answer goes (a new query, a typed edit, a closed box, an answer whose tables are narrower). It is a pure function of the answer being shown: nothing is remembered, so nothing can stay wide by mistake.

doc: The same rule for an ANSWER CARD (the hospital card's tables, the table of a model-written or finder answer): I widen the box for 4 or more columns and a row (my reason, 23 Nov 2026: a weekly OPD schedule of seven columns was cramped). It is a pure function of the answer on screen, so the box narrows again when the answer goes.

behaviours: no answer: normal width
no tables: normal width
a 2-column table: normal width
a 3-column table: normal width
a 4-column table with rows: wide
a 5-column table with rows: wide
a 4-column table with no rows: normal width
the second table alone can widen it
missing columns do not throw
card: no answer / no table: normal
card: hospital table of 4+ columns: wide (the weekly OPD schedule has 7)
card: hospital table of 2 columns: normal
card: a wide extra table widens it
card: a model/finder table of 4+ columns: wide, of 3: normal
the box width is computed from the synthesis shown now (and from a calculator page that asks for the wide box: toolWidth.selftest.ts)
the wide box is exactly the page's width (--omni-page-width), and no other box is wider than the page
the box's row leaves the scrollbar's room on its right, so the box and the page behind share one centre
the blur covers only the page's footprint; the dimming covers the screen (a screen-wide blur smeared the page's dark edge outside the box)
the text scale of the card is the screen's scale times MODAL_TEXT_FACTOR (3% smaller), in the wide box and in the normal box alike
the stored text scale state (omniK) is not changed by the factor (the factor is applied only where the variable is set)
no fixed wide width is left in the modal (76rem / 88vw / 96vw / 2000px)
--omni-page-width is the full width below md and --content-width from md up
the page wrappers use the same breakpoint rule (w-full md:w-[var(--content-width)])
nothing stores the wide state (no useState for it)
the text scale does not follow the wide state
